Subject: Sterling Health RFP — assurance matrix / sampling details

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the overview last week. Sterling's security and model governance committee asked us to get a concise technical annex that maps Redwood's controls to NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act plus a concrete evaluation / regression-sampling plan we can review with our auditors.

Specifically, they'd like:
- A control mapping (NIST AI RMF functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, etc.) showing which Redwood features and artifacts satisfy each control.
- Redwood's position on EU AI Act risk class assignment for the models we discussed and what mitigations you treat as operational controls versus product features.
- A sampling methodology for production regression checks and post-deploy monitoring (how many samples, stratification, retrain/rollback criteria).

Can you provide a short annex and an example sampling plan we can include in the RFP? We are on a tight cadence — our internal deadline for submission is 2026-12-08.

Thanks,

Sr. Vendor Risk Manager
Sterling Health

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sterling Health RFP — assurance matrix / sampling details

Claire —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached an initial assurance matrix and a concise evaluation-sampling plan for your review (Assurance_Matrix_Redwood_v1.xlsx; Eval_Sampling_Plan_Redwood.pdf). High-level points below; the attachments contain the tabular mapping and concrete numbers.

1) NIST AI RMF mapping- We map Redwood controls to NIST functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, and Protect). The assurance matrix ties each control to: configuration options, required artifacts (model-card, eval-suite, baseline metrics), and operational evidence (audit logs, route-level SLOs, and rollout policies). Example: for 'Measure' we provide token-level latency/cost traces, per-route quality dashboards, and the regression-harness outputs stored for 90 days (configurable).

2) EU AI Act position- For the model classes discussed in the RFP, Redwood assesses them as 'high-risk' for regulated clinical-assistants and 'limited-risk' for internal summarization tools. We treat EU-mandated mitigations in two buckets:
  - Product-level mitigations (built into the runtime): guardrails, function-calling schema enforcement, deterministic output options for structured tasks.
  - Operational controls (customer-facing): evaluation certification, deployment gating, documented human oversight procedures, and customer-configurable data retention/KMS hooks.

3) Evaluation & regression sampling approach (summary)- Our recommended approach is in the attached PDF. Summary:
  - Baseline definition: establish a production baseline from a three-week stabilized window after initial rollout.
  - Sampling strategy: stratified sampling by intent (top 8 intents for early production) + distributional buckets by prompt length and user cohort.
  - Sample size: for initial monthly checks we propose 1,000 labeled production examples per major intent bucket or a minimum of 5,000 total samples (whichever is greater).
  - Regression criteria: automated regression checks include per-unit metric shifts (ROUGE/EM/KL where applicable) and utility deltas (user completion rate). We use a two-tier threshold: warning at p-value < 0.05 / metric drift > 2% and fail at p-value < 0.01 / metric drift > 5%, with an SLO for human review turnaround within 48 hours.
  - Continuous monitoring: real-time alerts for sharp distributional shifts (population-level drift), and weekly aggregate reports.

4) Third-party audits & evidence- We provide exportable artifacts: model-card, eval-suite runs, audit log export (syslog + structured JSON), and a hashed sample store for auditor verification. We are open to scoped third-party review; we can coordinate the access model (time-limited credentials + redacted datasets).

Next steps: if you'd like, Neha (cc'd) can join a 30-min call to walk the audit team through the matrix and sampling plan later this week. We can also produce a 'low-touch' version of the matrix that maps to ISO/SOC controls if your procurement team needs it.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Claire —

Thanks for the follow-up. Quick answers and a concrete example below; we can go deeper on the call if helpful.

1) Representative production slices (example for a healthcare assistant)  - Intents: appointment_scheduling, medication_lookup, symptom_triage, billing_question, discharge_instructions, clinical_summary_request, referral_help, admin_misc.  - Cohorts: patient_vintage (new vs returning), channel (mobile/web), geography/region, payer_type.  - Example stratification: sample proportional to traffic but enforce a minimum per-stratum floor (n=50) to ensure power for long-tail categories. In practice: if appointment_scheduling is 40% of traffic and symptom_triage is 10%, the monthly sample allocation (for 5,000 total) would be ~2,000 and ~500 respectively, but with the 50-floor rule for smaller slices.

2) Sample-size scaling for long-tail intents  - Approach: hierarchical pooling and adaptive allocation. Start with a conservative floor (50–100 labeled items) for long-tail intents. Use Bayesian shrinkage to borrow strength from similar intents when computing drift metrics. For acceptance criteria: smaller buckets have wider credible intervals; we flag persistent drift (3 consecutive months) rather than single-month variance.

3) Third-party auditor access model  - We supply time-limited read-only access to a redacted dataset and hashed sample store. Exportable artifacts include: evaluation-suite runs (deterministic seeds), model-card, audit-log exports (redaction applies to PII and PHI — we provide synthetic anonymized variants plus hash references so auditors can verify integrity).  - NDA/process: we have a standard vendor-audit addendum; sample redaction policy attached. For full audits, we typically coordinate through a scoping call and provide a dedicated SSO-enabled account with IP restrictions for the audit window.

Concrete sample-size example (attached in Eval_Sampling_Plan_Redwood.pdf): for an initial monthly health-check at 5,000 samples across N=8 major intents we propose:  - Top 3 intents: 800–1,500 samples each  - Mid intents: 300–700  - Tail intents: 50–200 (with pooling)

We can present these slides to your audit committee and share the redaction template. Markus — I'm available for a 30-min slot tomorrow 09:00–11:30 PST; Marissa, can you join to cover contractual/IRT items?

Neha Kapoor
